newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends up and within recent range.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends up and within recent range.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed slightly higher, buoyed by trade buying in May and speculative buying in July, trading sources said.
The trade was a noted buyer of the May/July spread, which remained steady from 0.26 to 0.24 throughout the day. The spread closed at 0.25 cent.
May ended up 0.04 at 11.00 cents, having ranged from 11.06 to 10.94. The back months closed 0.05 firmer to 0.01 weaker.
Volume was estimated at 17,114 lots compared to Wednesday's official 14,882 lots.

Benchmark May pierced its recent high of 11.04 and climbed to the day's high of 11.06, where the trade became an aggressive seller. The selling blunted several attempts to move higher throughout the day, dealers said.
One floor source said trading in the May/October spread out to 0.44 was encouraging and suggests the trade has more short-covering to do in the near term.

Meantime, open interest in May rose 548 lots to 60,495 lots as of Wednesday's close, indicating that the speculators are in no hurry to liquidate long positions ahead of the contract's expiry. The last trading day for May is April 30.
"We could work higher," a trader said, noting that the market has not followed its recent trend of falling back into the 10.70-cent-per-lb range basis May, after climbing to top of the recent range.
He said May could test 11.15 over the next week and fall back into a 10.50-11.00 cent trading range ahead of the expiry of May options on Friday, April 11.
The 10.50 puts and 11.00 calls have the largest open interest.
Nearby support was pegged at Tuesday's low of 10.78 cents basis May.

In fundamental news, Brazilian government officals and industry representatives today outlined criteria for the 1997/98 sugar crop plan. Among the provisions was that no alcohol will be imported during the year.

Last year, Brazil imported about 400 million liters of alcohol, Pedro Cabral, head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's sugar and alcohol department, said. Brazil produced about 290 million tonnes of cane, he added.
